keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Western Yan shape begins in 387, but the state starts in 384 east of Tong Pass (Hong defeated a Qin force at Huayin) and takes Chang'an in 385. The infobox gives no area; the disc round Chang'an is a placeholder for a roving army.

correction.text: Zhangzi (modern Changzhi) and the Shanxi land the Xianbei settled in 386

keyframe_review.note: 387-389, 116,090 km2 at 110.5-115.0 E, 35.1-40.0 N (Shanxi): right land, a year late. The Xianbei 'headed east back toward their homeland, but eventually settled down in modern Shanxi'; Yong took Zhangzi in 386 and declared himself emperor, so the shape holds from 386. The page names Shanxi, Beidi and Pingyang (Linfen) but no commanderies and gives no area; ratio unavailable.
390-391, 116,040 km2, the same Shanxi shape. The page records no change of land in these years (rulers and wars only).

392-393, 116,040 km2, the same shape; the state lasts to 394: In 394, Murong Chui led an attack and besieged Zhangzi. Yong was captured and killed, ending Western Yan. Cliopatria's Later Yan shape takes the land from 394.

region.text: east of Tong Pass at Huayin

ledger.note: 384: Murong Hong founds the Western Yan east of Tong Pass. 'It was founded by Murong Hong in 384 in the aftermath of the Former Qin's defeat' at Fei River; the Sixteen Kingdoms page: 'Western Yan (384-394)'. The page names no founding place beyond the Huayin fight.

region.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley round it

ledger.note: 385: Murong Chong takes Chang'an. He besieged the city and, 'in 385', after Murong Wei's execution, claimed the title of emperor (27 January 385); the page dates the capture only to 385. The Sixteen Kingdoms page: 'In 385, the Western Yan ousted Fu Jian from Chang'an'.

region.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley round it

ledger.note: 386: the Xianbei abandon Chang'an. Infobox 'Abandonment of Chang'an: 386'; the people headed east. The Sixteen Kingdoms table gives Later Qin's capital as Chang'an from 386 and the Later Qin dossier records Yao Chang's occupation; this page names no taker.

region.text: Zhangzi (modern Changzhi) and the Shanxi land the Xianbei settled in 386

ledger.note: 386: Murong Yong takes Zhangzi and declares himself emperor. Yong took Fu Pi's capital at Zhangzi ('in modern Changzhi, Shanxi'); the Xianbei 'eventually settled down in modern Shanxi'. The page names Shanxi, Beidi and Pingyang (Linfen) and no commanderies.
386: the capital is Zhangzi, where it stays to 394 (infobox Zhangzi 386-394).

394: Murong Chui destroys the Western Yan at Zhangzi. In 394, Murong Chui led an attack and besieged Zhangzi. Yong was captured and killed, ending Western Yan; the Sixteen Kingdoms page: Chui 'conquered the Western Yan in 394'. The page gives no month.

wars.name: Western Yan siege of Chang'an

zones.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley round it

wars.outcome: Murong Chui besieged Zhangzi; Murong Yong was captured and killed, ending the state; Later Yan had pacified Hebei after 392 when Yong failed to relieve Zhai Wei.

certainty.note: The page gives Chang'an, Zhangzi and 'modern Shanxi' only; no frontier is drawn from any treaty or survey.

notes: Cliopatria row: Western Yan 387..393 (three shapes, 116,090 and 116,040 km2, all the same Shanxi outline). (1) The state lives 384-394: Cliopatria misses 384-386 (Huayin, Chang'an, the move east) and ends one year early (Later Yan's shape takes the land in 394). (2) The page does not date the Xianbei's departure from Chang'an inside 386 or the taking of Zhangzi inside 386; both are 386 at confidence 2, no month. (3) Fu Pi's capital at Zhangzi is the page's wording; Former Qin's dossier has Fu Pi at Jinyang in 385-386, so Zhangzi's previous holder is named former-qin for the whole remnant. (4) Undated wars on the page, not in the ledger: a brief fight with Later Qin, and Yong's failed attempt on Luoyang against Eastern Jin. (5) Not among the Sixteen Kingdoms by tradition (Sixteen Kingdoms page: 'not listed among the Sixteen Kingdom'). (6) Zhangzi (Changzhi) is in the south-east of Shanxi while Cliopatria's shape is centred on Taiyuan-Linfen; the page does not settle the extent, so the shape stays. Cross-dossier gap: the Former Qin dossier has the loss of Chang'an to the Western Yan in 385 but none for Zhangzi in 386, and the Later Qin dossier's 386 gain of Chang'an names the Western Yan as the previous holder.
